title: Offline and Progressive Web Applications knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Offline and Progressive Web Applications”?
options: Offline and Progressive Web Applications helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Offline and Progressive Web Applications means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Offline and Progressive Web Applications removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Offline and Progressive Web Applications should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Offline and Progressive Web Applications helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Offline and Progressive Web Applications is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Progressive web application fundamentals” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Progressive web application fundamentals” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Progressive web application fundamentals” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Progressive web application fundamentals” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Progressive web application fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Progressive web application fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Progressive web application fundamentals” under Offline and Progressive Web Applications. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Offline and Progressive Web Applications”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
